rows.reason: parseRun is only ever called on records returned by records.readMany (plan-readers.ts:1308, :1456), and both production backends decode and apply the registered RunSnapshot@1 schema before returning ready (sqlite-record-store.ts:375-386; in-memory-record-store.ts:248-252). validateRunSnapshot (materials/record-readers.ts:186-268) is strictly stronger than parseRun: it already requires a parsed object (:190-191), a complete RunRef (:194), the exact refKey (:195-196), the task triple (:217-224), a non-empty attemptId (:225), a legal status (:248) and a same-project PlanRevisionRef (:226-229). A body that fails any of these is refused upstream as corrupt (sqlite-record-store.ts:383-385), so a ready record can never take the `parsed === null` arm at 1131. Claude's U assumes a damaged record reaches the reader, but the store stops it first.
rows.proposal: Delete the duplicate JSON/ref/shape failure path in parseRun (1131-1139) and trust the store-validated ready record; the `run === null` branches at 1309, 1457, 1668 and 2061 then go. A damaged body remains the store's `corrupt` result (sqlite-record-store.ts:383-385), handled as non-ready before parsing.

So the `continue` arm at 1390 is reachable only through a record written outside the platform's writers (a hand-edited store or a foreign writer), never through public steps. That is U, not D2: the codec does not exclude the shape, the only-writer argument does.
rows.proposal: Keep the `phase !== 'satisfied'` filter untested (AGENTS rule 4: no tamper test). It guards the still-four-valued TaskReductionPhase contract (contracts/reduction.ts:24; plan-readers.ts:147, :214); narrowing that contract to 'satisfied' and then deleting the filter is a separate, larger decision, not required by this row.
